paragraphs: We are a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming the treatment of rare diseases.
We have three approved medicines: LIVMARLI® (maralixibat) ("Livmarli"), CHOLBAM® (cholic acid) capsules ("Cholbam"), and CTEXLI® (chenodiol) tablets ("Ctexli").

Livmarli is a novel, orally administered, minimally-absorbed ileal bile acid transporter ("IBAT") inhibitor ("IBATi") that is approved for the treatment of cholestatic pruritus in patients with Alagille syndrome ("ALGS") in the United States ("U.S."), the European Union ("EU") and various other countries around the world and for cholestatic pruritus in patients with progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis ("PFIC") in the U.S., Canada and Japan and for the treatment of PFIC in the EU. We market and commercialize Livmarli in the U.S., Canada and certain countries in Europe through our specialized and focused commercial team. We have also entered into license and distribution agreements with several rare disease companies for the commercialization of Livmarli in additional countries. We are also seeking to add to the approved indications for Livmarli by conducting the EXPAND study in settings of cholestatic pruritus due to other rare conditions.

In August 2023, we completed the acquisition of assets of Travere Therapeutics, Inc. ("Travere") that are primarily related to the development, manufacture (including synthesis, formulation, finishing or packaging) and commercialization of chenodiol and Cholbam (also known as Kolbam) (and together with chenodiol, the "Bile Acid Medicines") pursuant to an asset purchase agreement dated July 16, 2023 (such acquisition, the "Bile Acid Portfolio Acquisition").

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") approved Cholbam in March 2015 as the first FDA-approved treatment for pediatric and adult patients with bile acid synthesis disorders due to single enzyme defects and for adjunctive treatment of patients with peroxisomal disorders, including peroxisome biogenesis disorder-Zellweger spectrum disorder ("PBD-ZSD"). Chenodiol is standard of care for the treatment of cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis ("CTX") in the U.S. with a medical necessity recognition by the FDA and was commercialized under the brand name Chenodal. We submitted a New Drug Application ("NDA") for chenodiol for the treatment of CTX in 2024 and received FDA approval for the treatment of adults with CTX in February 2025. Chenodiol is commercialized under the brand name Ctexli. We currently market and commercialize Cholbam and Ctexli in the U.S. through our specialized and focused commercial team. We have also assumed license and distribution agreements with several rare disease companies for the commercialization of Cholbam and chenodiol in additional countries.

We are advancing our product candidate, volixibat, a novel, oral, minimally-absorbed agent designed to inhibit IBAT, for the treatment of adult patients with cholestatic liver diseases. We are developing volixibat in the setting of primary sclerosing cholangitis ("PSC") and primary biliary cholangitis ("PBC"). Volixibat has received FDA breakthrough therapy and orphan drug designation for cholestatic pruritus in PBC patients based on the positive interim analysis of the VANTAGE Phase 2b study. Volixibat has also completed a successful interim analysis of the VISTAS Phase 2b study in PSC patients. Enrollment of our VISTAS Phase 2b clinical trial in PSC was completed in the third quarter of 2025 and we expect to announce top-line results from this trial in the second quarter of 2026. Enrollment of our VANTAGE Phase 2b clinical trial in PBC is expected to be completed in the second half of 2026.

On January 23, 2026, we completed the acquisition of Bluejay Therapeutics, Inc. ("Bluejay" and such acquisition, the "Bluejay Acquisition") and its lead product candidate brelovitug (BJT-778). We are advancing brelovitug for the treatment of chronic hepatitis D virus ("HDV") infection. Brelovitug is a fully human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds the hepatitis B surface antigen, thereby clearing virions and subviral particles and preventing HDV infection and replication. Brelovitug has been granted FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation and European Medicines Agency ("EMA") Priority Medicines ("PRIME") scheme designation and European Commission orphan medicinal product designation. Brelovitug is currently being evaluated in the global AZURE clinical program with topline results from the AZURE-1 and AZURE-4 registration-enabling clinical trials expected in the second half of 2026.

We are also advancing our product candidate MRM-3379, a novel, oral, CNS-penetrant PDE4D inhibitor for the treatment of fragile X syndrome ("FXS"). We are currently enrolling patients in the BLOOM Phase 2 clinical study of MRM-3379 in FXS and expect topline data in 2027.
Our goal is to strengthen our leadership position in rare and orphan diseases for which the unmet medical need is high. The key components of our strategy include:

•Commercialize medicines for rare diseases. Livmarli is approved by the FDA and the European Commission for the treatment of cholestatic pruritus in patients with ALGS, approved by the FDA for treatment of cholestatic pruritus in patients with PFIC and approved by EMA for the treatment of PFIC. We are commercializing Livmarli in the United States, Canada, and certain countries in Europe through direct sales. Additionally, we have entered into several distributor and licensing agreements to advance Livmarli in numerous territories outside of the markets where we commercialize Livmarli directly. Chenodiol is standard of care in the U.S. for the treatment of CTX and is being commercialized under the brand name Ctexli. Cholbam is approved for the treatment of bile acid synthesis disorders and adjunctive treatment of patients with peroxisomal disorders, including PBD-ZSD and we expect to continue to commercialize the medicine for these indications. We are commercializing Ctexli and Cholbam in the United States through one specialty pharmacy.

•Advance our current pipeline of clinical programs to regulatory approval. We are seeking to add to the approved indications for Livmarli by conducting the EXPAND study in settings of cholestatic pruritus due to other rare conditions. We plan to further leverage our understanding of cholestatic liver disease with volixibat in adult settings. We are conducting adaptive, potentially registrational, Phase 2b clinical trials of volixibat in PSC and PBC. We acquired Bluejay in January 2026 and plan to continue to develop brelovitug for the treatment of chronic HDV infection. We are conducting the global AZURE program to enable registration in the U.S., Europe and other geographies. MRM-3379 is a novel PDE4D inhibitor, which we expect to develop for FXS, a rare genetic neurocognitive disorder. We initiated a dose ranging Phase 2 trial in 2025 with data expected in 2027.

•Continue to acquire additional pipeline or commercial rare disease products or companies. We have assembled a team of scientific, clinical and business leaders with highly relevant experience to enable the advancement of therapeutics for rare and orphan diseases. We intend to leverage our collective expertise to identify, acquire, in-license and advance additional product candidates for the treatment of rare and orphan diseases.

•Deploy our resources efficiently to maximize value creation and long term financial performance. Our financial objective is value creation through long-term cash-flow generating revenue growth. We aim to accomplish this by successfully commercializing current approved medicines and successfully developing and commercializing current and future clinical-stage product candidates.

headings: Risks Related to Commercialization of our Approved Medicines and Development of our Product Candidates
The success of our business depends, in part, on our ability to market and sell our approved medicines profitably.

Our commercial success may be severely hindered if we are unable to obtain and/or maintain adequate coverage and reimbursement for our approved medicines and any future product candidates, if approved.

Our approved medicines or any one of our product candidates, if approved, may fail to achieve the market acceptance among physicians, patients and others in the medical community necessary for commercial success.
We may face product liability exposure, and if claims are brought against us, we may incur substantial liability if our insurance coverage for those claims is inadequate.

Our business depends, in part, on the success of our product candidates, each of which requires significant clinical testing before we can seek regulatory approval and potentially launch commercial sales.

We have encountered and may continue to encounter delays and difficulties enrolling patients in our clinical trials, and as a result, our clinical development activities could be delayed or otherwise adversely affected.
Our clinical trials may fail to adequately demonstrate the safety and efficacy of our product candidates, which could prevent or delay regulatory approval and commercialization.
Clinical drug development involves a lengthy and expensive process with uncertain outcomes, and results of earlier studies and trials may not be predictive of future trial results.

You should consider all of the risk factors described when evaluating our business.

The success of our business depends, in part, on our ability to commercialize our approved medicines profitably. Our successful commercialization of our approved medicines depends on a number of factors, including, among others, the following:

•our ability to grow and maintain our sales team in the U.S., Canada, and certain countries in Europe, as well as scale our distribution capabilities in these locations and others where our products are available;
•the availability of adequate reimbursement and a commercially viable sales price of our approved medicines;
•acceptance by physicians, payors and patients of the benefits, safety and efficacy of our approved medicines, including relative to alternative and competing treatments;
•a continued acceptable safety profile of our approved medicines;

paragraphs: You should read the following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations together with our consolidated financial statements and related notes included in Item 8 "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" and included elsewhere in this Annual Report. This discussion and analysis contains forward-looking statements based upon our current beliefs, estimates, plans and expectations that involve risks, uncertainties and assumptions. Our actual results may differ materially from those contained in these forward-looking statements as a result of various factors, including those set forth under "Risk Factors" or in other parts of this Annual Report.

We are a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming the treatment of rare diseases. We have three approved medicines: LIVMARLI® (maralixibat) ("Livmarli"), CHOLBAM® (cholic acid) capsules ("Cholbam"), and CTEXLI® (chenodiol) tablets ("Ctexli").

Livmarli is a novel, orally administered, minimally-absorbed ileal bile acid transporter ("IBAT") inhibitor ("IBATi") that is approved for the treatment of cholestatic pruritus in patients with Alagille syndrome ("ALGS") in the United States ("U.S."), the European Union ("EU") and various other countries around the world and for cholestatic pruritus in patients with progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis ("PFIC") in the U.S., Canada and Japan and for the treatment of PFIC in the EU. We market and commercialize Livmarli in the U.S., Canada and certain countries in Europe through our specialized and focused commercial team. We have also entered into license and distribution agreements with several rare disease companies for the commercialization of Livmarli in additional countries. In March 2025, our partner Takeda received approval from the Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour, and Welfare for Livmarli for the treatment of cholestatic pruritus in patients with ALGS and PFIC.

In August 2023, we completed the acquisition of assets of Travere Therapeutics, Inc. ("Travere") that are primarily related to the development, manufacture (including synthesis, formulation, finishing or packaging) and commercialization of chenodiol and Cholbam (also known as Kolbam) (and together with chenodiol, the "Bile Acid Medicines") pursuant to an asset purchase agreement dated July 16, 2023 (such acquisition, the "Bile Acid Portfolio Acquisition").

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") approved Cholbam in March 2015, as the first FDA-approved treatment for pediatric and adult patients with bile acid synthesis disorders due to single enzyme defects, and for adjunctive treatment of patients with peroxisomal disorders, including peroxisome biogenesis disorder-Zellweger spectrum disorder ("PBD-ZSD"). Chenodiol is standard of care for the treatment of cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis ("CTX") in the U.S. with a medical necessity recognition by the FDA and was commercialized under the brand name Chenodal. We submitted a new drug application ("NDA") for chenodiol for the treatment of CTX in 2024 and received FDA approval for the treatment of adults with CTX in February 2025, which is commercialized under the brand name Ctexli. We currently market and commercialize Cholbam and Ctexli in the U.S. through our specialized and focused commercial team. We have also assumed license and distribution agreements with several rare disease companies for the commercialization of Cholbam and chenodiol in additional countries.

We are advancing our product candidate, volixibat, a novel, oral, minimally-absorbed agent designed to inhibit IBAT, for the treatment of adult patients with cholestatic liver diseases. We are developing volixibat in the setting of primary sclerosing cholangitis ("PSC") and primary biliary cholangitis ("PBC"), and in October 2024, we announced that the FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy designation for volixibat as a potential treatment for cholestatic pruritus in patients with PBC. We conducted an interim analysis of our VISTAS Phase 2b clinical trial in PSC and reported interim data from our VANTAGE Phase 2b clinical trial in PBC in June 2024. The VISTAS Phase 2b clinical trial in PSC completed enrollment in the third quarter of 2025 and topline data is expected in the second quarter of 2026. In addition, we expect to submit an NDA to the FDA for volixibat for the treatment of PSC in the second half of 2026, with both potential approval and subsequent launch of volixibat for the treatment of PSC, if approved, to occur in the first half of 2027. We expect the VANTAGE Phase 2b clinical trial in PBC to complete enrollment in the second half of 2026 with topline data expected in the first half of 2027.

In addition, we are developing Livmarli for certain rare cholestatic conditions through the Phase 3 EXPAND study, which we initiated in the fourth quarter of 2024. We expect to complete enrollment of the EXPAND study in the first half of 2026 with topline data expected in the fourth quarter of 2026.

In October 2024, we completed a license agreement with Enthorin Therapeutics, LLC and Dart Neuroscience LLC granting us the worldwide right to develop and commercialize MRM-3379, an allosteric inhibitor of Phosphodiesterase 4D ("PDE4D"). We are currently enrolling patients in the BLOOM Phase 2 clinical study of MRM-3379 in Fragile-X Syndrome ("FXS") and expect topline data in 2027.

On January 23, 2026, we completed the acquisition (the "Bluejay Acquisition") of Bluejay Therapeutics, Inc. ("Bluejay") and its lead product candidate brelovitug (BJT-778). We are advancing brelovitug for the treatment of chronic hepatitis D virus ("HDV") infection. Brelovitug is a fully human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds the hepatitis B surface antigen, thereby clearing virions and subviral particles and preventing HDV infection and replication. Brelovitug has been granted FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation, EMA Priority Medicines ("PRIME") scheme designation and European Commission orphan medicinal product designation. Brelovitug is currently being evaluated in the global AZURE clinical program with topline results from the AZURE-1 and AZURE-4 registration-enabling clinical trials expected in the second half of 2026 and top-line results from the AZURE-2 and AZURE-3 registration-enabling clinical trials expected by the first half of 2028. We believe that the results from the AZURE-1 and AZURE-4 trials may support a potential biologics license application submission to the FDA for brelovitug in HDV in the first half of 2027 followed by a potential approval and subsequent launch, if approved, in the second half of 2027. We believe that the results of the AZURE-2 and AZURE-3 clinical trials may support a potential EMA registration and subsequent commercial launch, if approved, in the EU.

To date, we have focused primarily on acquiring and in-licensing our product candidates, organizing and staffing our company, business planning, raising capital, advancing our product candidates through clinical development, preparing for commercialization of our product candidates, commercializing our approved medicines, and conducting business development activities relating to, among other things, portfolio expansion through collaborations and acquisitions.

Our net loss was $23.4 million and $87.9 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $667.5 million compared to $644.2 million as of December 31, 2024. As of December 31, 2025, we had unrestricted cash, cash equivalents and investments of $391.4 million, compared to $292.8 million as of December 31, 2024.

While we generated net income in the third quarter of 2025, we anticipate we will continue to generate net losses for the foreseeable future as we continue commercial activities for our approved medicines, conduct our ongoing and planned clinical trials, including the clinical trials for brelovitug, seek regulatory approvals for our product candidates and make potential milestone payments to the licensors and other third parties from whom we have in-licensed or acquired our product candidates. We expect that total product sales of our approved medicines will continue to increase on an annual basis; however, due to large periodic orders from Takeda and our distributors, our product revenue may experience quarterly fluctuations. Additionally, our product revenues from Takeda are based upon variable consideration estimates. If actual results vary from our estimates, we will make adjustments in the period when such variances become known. As a result, our net losses may fluctuate significantly from quarter-to-quarter and year-to-year.

We expect to satisfy future cash needs through existing capital balances, revenue from our approved medicines and through a combination of equity offerings, debt financings or other capital sources, collaborations, licenses and other similar arrangements. However, we may be unable to raise additional funds or enter into such other arrangements when needed on favorable terms or at all. Our failure to raise capital or enter into such other arrangements when needed could have a negative impact on our financial condition and on our ability to pursue our business plans and strategies. If we are unable to raise additional capital when needed, we could be forced to delay, limit, reduce or terminate the development of one or more of our product candidates or future commercialization efforts or grant rights to develop and market our product candidates even if we would otherwise prefer to develop and market such product candidates ourselves.

In October 2024, we completed the in-license of MRM-3379. We paid a one-time non-refundable license fee of $7.5 million upon closing of the transaction, and up to an additional $217.5 million is payable upon achievement of certain development, regulatory and commercial milestones.

paragraphs: 本公司為一間專注於改變罕見疾病治療方式的生技藥品公司。
本公司已核准上市之藥品有三種：LIVMARLI®（maralixibat）（"Livmarli"）、CHOLBAM®（cholic acid）膠囊（"Cholbam"）及 CTEXLI®（chenodiol）片劑（"Ctexli"）。

Livmarli 是一種新型口服、吸收率低的回腸膽固醇運輸體（"IBAT"）抑制劑（"IBATi"），已核准用於治療患有阿加利 syndrome（"ALGS"）之患者之膽汁淤積性癢症，於美國（"U.S."）、歐盟（"EU"）及世界各地多個國家，以及用於治療患有進行性家族性肝內膽汁淤積症（"PFIC"）之患者之膽汁淤積性癢症，於美國、加拿大及日本，並於歐盟核准用於治療 PFIC。本公司透過專門且聚焦之商業團隊，在美國、加拿大及歐洲部分國家行銷與販售 Livmarli。本公司亦已與多家罕見疾病公司簽訂授權與分銷協議，以在更多國家進行 Livmarli 之商業化。本公司亦正尋求增加 Livmarli 之核准適應症，透過 EXPAND 研究於其他罕見疾病所致之膽汁淤積性癢症環境中進行。
2023 年 8 月，本公司完成取得 Travere Therapeutics, Inc.（"Travere"）之資產，這些資產主要與 chenodiol 及 Cholbam（亦稱 Kolbam）之開發、製造（包括合成、製備、完成或包裝）及商業化有關，根據 2023 年 7 月 16 日簽訂之資產買賣協議（此筆買賣，稱為 "Bile Acid Portfolio Acquisition"）。

美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）於 2015 年 3 月核准 Cholbam，作為首個 FDA 核准用於治療因單一酵素缺陷所致之膽固醇合成障礙之兒童及成人患者，以及作為 peroxisomal 障礙患者之輔助治療，包括 peroxisome 生成障礙症-Zellweger 節譜系障礙（"PBD-ZSD"）患者。Chenodiol 是美國治療腦動脈硬化性黃瘤（"CTX"）的標準療法，並經 FDA 認可其醫療必要性，且曾以 Chenodal 品牌進行商業化。本公司於 2024 年提交 chenodiol 用於治療 CTX 之新藥申請（"NDA"），並於 2025 年 2 月獲得 FDA 核准用於治療 CTX 之成人患者。Chenodiol 以 Ctexli 品牌進行商業化。本公司目前透過專門且聚焦之商業團隊，在美國行銷與販售 Cholbam 及 Ctexli。本公司亦已承接與多家罕見疾病公司之授權與分銷協議，以在更多國家進行 Cholbam 及 chenodiol 之商業化。

本公司正在推進產品候選藥物 volixibat，一種新型口服、吸收率低之藥物，設計用於治療患有膽汁淤積性肝病之成人患者。本公司正在 PSC（原發性硬化性膽管炎）及 PBC（原發性膽管炎）環境中開發 volixibat。Volixibat 已獲 FDA 突破性療法及罕見疾病藥物指定，用於 PBC 患者之膽汁淤積性癢症，基於 VANTAGE 第二期雙盲試驗之正面中期分析結果。Volixibat 亦已完成 PSC 患者之 VISTAS 第二期雙盲試驗之成功中期分析。本公司於 2025 年第三季完成 VISTAS 第二期雙盲臨牀試驗之入組，預計於 2026 年第二季公佈此試驗之主要結果。本公司預計於 2026 年第二季完成 VANTAGE 第二期雙盲臨牀試驗之入組。

本公司於 2026 年 1 月 23 日完成取得 Bluejay Therapeutics, Inc.（"Bluejay"）及其主要產品候選藥物 brelovitug（BJT-778）之買賣（此筆買賣稱為 "Bluejay Acquisition"）。本公司正在推進 brelovitug 用於治療慢性乙型肝炎 D 病毒（"HDV"）感染。Brelovitug 是一種完全人源 IgG1 單克隆抗體，可與乙型肝炎表面抗原結合，從而清除病毒顆粒及亞病毒顆粒，並防止 HDV 感染及複製。Brelovitug 已獲 FDA 突破性療法指定及歐洲藥物管理局（"EMA"）優先藥物（"PRIME"）方案指定及歐洲委員會罕見藥物指定。Brelovitug 目前正在全球 AZURE 臨牀計畫中評估，預計於 2026 年第二季公佈 AZURE-1 及 AZURE-4 登記性臨牀試驗之主要結果。
本公司亦正在推進產品候選藥物 MRM-3379，一種新型口服、能穿透 CNS（大腦與神經系統）之 PDE4D 抑制劑，用於治療脆性 X 綜合症（"FXS"）。本公司目前正在 FXS 進行 BLOOM 第二期臨牀試驗之患者入組，預計於 2027 年公佈主要數據。
本公司目標為強化在罕見及罕見疾病領域的領導地位，尤其針對醫療需求未被滿足之情形。我們策略的關鍵零組件包括：

•推廣用於罕見疾病的藥物。Livmarli 已經獲得 FDA 與歐盟委員會核准，用於治療 ALGS 患者之膽汁淤積性癢症，並獲得 FDA 核准用於治療 PFIC 患者之膽汁淤積性癢症，且獲得 EMA 核准用於治療 PFIC。本公司正在美國、加拿大及歐洲部分國家透過直接銷售方式推廣 Livmarli。此外，本公司已與多家經銷商及授權合作夥伴簽訂協議，以推廣 Livmarli 至本公司直接銷售市場以外的多個地區。Chenodiol 在美國為治療 CTX 的標準療法，並以品牌名稱 Ctexli 進行推廣。Cholbam 已核准用於治療膽汁酸合成障礙，並作為過氧化物酶體障礙患者（包括 PBD-ZSD）的輔助治療，本公司預期會持續推廣此藥物用於這些適應症。本公司正在美國透過一家專門藥房推廣 Ctexli 和 Cholbam。

•持續推動目前臨牀計畫進度，以取得監管核准。我們正尋求為Livmarli增加核准適應症，透過在其他罕見疾病引起的膽汁淤積性癢症環境中進行EXPAND研究來實現。我們計畫進一步運用對膽汁淤積性肝病的瞭解，於成人環境中使用volixibat。我們正在進行適應性、可能具註冊意義的Phase 2b臨牀試驗，用於PSC和PBC的volixibat。我們於2026年1月收購Bluejay，並計畫持續開發brelovitug用於治療慢性HDV感染。我們正在進行全球AZURE計畫，以實現美國、歐洲及其他地區的註冊。MRM-3379是一種新型PDE4D抑制劑，我們預期將其開發用於FXS，一種罕見的遺傳性神經認知障礙。我們於2025年啟動了一項劑量範圍Phase 2試驗，預計於2027年取得數據。
•持續取得更多管線或商業化罕見疾病的產品或公司。本公司已組建一支具高度相關經驗的科學、臨牀及商業領導團隊，以促進罕見及罕見疾病的治療藥物的發展。本公司計畫利用團隊的集體專業知識，識別、取得、授權進口並推進更多產品候選藥物，用於治療罕見及罕見疾病。
•有效運用資源以最大化價值創造及長期財務表現。本公司財務目標為透過長期現金流產生的收入成長來實現價值創造。本公司計畫透過成功商業化現有核准藥物，以及成功開發及商業化現有及未來臨牀階段產品候選藥物來達成此目標。

paragraphs: 您應閱讀下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，並與我們合併財務報表及相關附註，包含於第 8 項 "財務報表與補充資料"，以及本年度報告其他部分所載內容一併參考。此討論與分析包含根據我們目前信念、估計、計畫與預期所作之預測性陳述，這些陳述涉及風險、不確定性與假設。我們實際結果可能與這些預測性陳述所載內容有重大差異，原因包括但不限於 "風險因素" 或本年度報告其他部分所載因素。
我們是一家專注於改變罕見疾病治療方式的生物製藥公司。我們已核准之藥品有三種：LIVMARLI® (maralixibat) ("Livmarli"), CHOLBAM® (cholic acid) 膠囊 ("Cholbam"), 以及 CTEXLI® (chenodiol) 薄片 ("Ctexli")。

Livmarli 是一種新型口服、吸收量少的回腸膽酸運輸體 ("IBAT") 抑制劑 ("IBATi")，已核准用於治療患有阿爾岡 syndrome ("ALGS") 的患者之膽汁淤積性癢症，於美國 ("U.S.")、歐盟 ("EU") 及世界各地多個國家，以及用於治療患有進行性家族性肝內膽汁淤積症 ("PFIC") 的患者之膽汁淤積性癢症，於美國、加拿大與日本，並於歐盟核准用於治療 PFIC。我們透過專門且聚焦的商業團隊，在美國、加拿大與歐洲部分國家行銷與販售 Livmarli。我們也與多家罕見疾病公司簽訂授權與分銷協議，以在更多國家進行 Livmarli 的商業化。2025 年 3 月，我們的合作夥伴 Takeda 從日本厚生勞動省獲得核准，核准 Livmarli 用於治療患有 ALGS 與 PFIC 的患者之膽汁淤積性癢症。

2023 年 8 月，我們完成對 Travere Therapeutics, Inc. ("Travere") 資產的收購，這些資產主要與 chenodiol 與 Cholbam (也稱為 Kolbam) 的開發、製造 (包括合成、製劑、完成或包裝) 與商業化有關，根據 2023 年 7 月 16 日簽訂的資產買斷協議 (此收購稱為 "Bile Acid Portfolio Acquisition")。

美國食品藥物管理局 ("FDA") 於 2015 年 3 月核准 Cholbam，作為第一個 FDA 核准用於治療因單一酵素缺陷所致之膽酸合成障礙的兒童與成人患者，以及用於治療過氧化物酶體疾病患者的輔助治療，包括過氧化物酶體生物生成障礙-Zellweger 綜合症 ("PBD-ZSD")。Chenodiol 是治療美國患者之腦腱脂質沉著症 ("CTX") 的標準療法，並獲得 FDA 的醫療必要性認可，並以品牌名稱 Chenodal 進行商業化。我們於 2024 年提交 chenodiol 的新藥申請 ("NDA") 用於治療 CTX，並於 2025 年 2 月獲得 FDA 核准用於治療 CTX 的成人患者，此藥物以品牌名稱 Ctexli 進行商業化。我們目前透過專門且聚焦的商業團隊，在美國行銷與販售 Cholbam 與 Ctexli。我們也已承擔與多家罕見疾病公司簽訂的授權與分銷協議，以在更多國家進行 Cholbam 與 chenodiol 的商業化。

我們正在推進我們的產品候選藥物 volixibat，一種新型口服、吸收量少的藥物，設計用於抑制 IBAT，以治療患有膽汁淤積性肝病的成人患者。我們正在 PSC (原發性硬化性膽管炎) 與 PBC (原發性膽管炎) 的背景下開發 volixibat。2024 年 10 月，我們宣佈 FDA 授予 volixibat 突破性療法資格，作為治療 PBC 患者之膽汁淤積性癢症的潛在療法。我們對 VISTAS Phase 2b 臨牀試驗進行了中期分析，並在 2024 年 6 月報告了 VANTAGE Phase 2b 臨牀試驗在 PBC 中的中期數據。VISTAS Phase 2b 臨牀試驗在 PSC 中的入組於 2025 年第三季完成，預計 2026 年第二季公佈頂線數據。此外，我們預計於 2026 年第二季提交 volixibat 的 NDA 給 FDA，用於治療 PSC。若獲批准，volixibat 的批准與上市可能於 2027 年第一季進行。我們預計 VANTAGE Phase 2b 臨牀試驗在 PBC 中的入組於 2026 年第二季完成，頂線數據預計於 2027 年第一季公佈。
此外，我們正在透過 Phase 3 EXPAND 研究開發 Livmarli 用於某些罕見的膽汁淤積性疾病，我們於 2024 年第四季啟動了該研究。我們預計於 2026 年第一季完成 EXPAND 研究的入組，並於 2026 年第四季公佈頂線數據。

2024 年 10 月，我們與 Enthorin Therapeutics, LLC 與 Dart Neuroscience LLC 籤訂授權協議，取得全球開發與商業化 MRM-3379 的權利，MRM-3379 是 Phosphodiesterase 4D ("PDE4D") 的別構抑制劑。我們目前正在進行 BLOOM Phase 2 臨牀試驗，用於治療 Fragile-X 綜合症 ("FXS") 的患者，並預計於 2027 年公佈頂線數據。

於2026年1月23日，本公司完成對Bluejay Therapeutics, Inc.（"Bluejay"）及其主要產品候選藥物brelovitug（BJT-778）的收購（"Bluejay收購"）。本公司正推動brelovitug用於治療慢性乙型肝炎病毒（"HDV"）感染。brelovitug為一種全人源IgG1單株抗體，可與乙型肝炎表面抗原結合，從而清除病毒顆粒與亞病毒顆粒，並預防HDV感染與複製。brelovitug已獲美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）突破性療法指定、歐洲藥物管理局（EMA）優先藥物（"PRIME"）方案指定及歐洲委員會罕見疾病藥物指定。brelovitug目前正於全球AZURE臨牀計畫中進行評估，預計在2026年下半年將公佈AZURE-1與AZURE-4註冊性臨牀試驗的初步結果，並預計在2028年上半年公佈AZURE-2與AZURE-3註冊性臨牀試驗的初步結果。本公司認為AZURE-1與AZURE-4試驗的結果可能支持於2027年上半年提交brelovitug用於HDV的生物製品許可申請，若獲批准，則可能於2027年下半年進行上市與發售。本公司認為AZURE-2與AZURE-3臨牀試驗的結果可能支持於歐盟進行EMA註冊並隨後上市，若獲批准，則可能於歐盟進行上市。
截至目前為止，本公司主要致力於取得與取得我們的產品候選藥物、組織與聘僱本公司、業務規劃、籌集資金、推動我們的產品候選藥物進行臨牀開發、準備我們的產品候選藥物的商業化、商業化我們已核准的藥物，以及進行與產品組合擴張相關的業務發展活動，包括合作與收購等。
本公司淨虧損為2025年12月31日止年度為2,340萬美元，2024年12月31日止年度為8,790萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，本公司累計虧損為66,750萬美元，較2024年12月31日的64,420萬美元為高。截至2025年12月31日，本公司持有未受限制的現金、現金等價物及投資為39,140萬美元，較2024年12月31日的29,280萬美元為高。

雖然本公司在2025年第三季產生了淨收入，但本公司預期將持續產生淨虧損，至少在可預見的未來，因本公司持續進行已核准藥物的商業活動、進行我們的持續及計畫中的臨牀試驗，包括brelovitug的臨牀試驗、尋求我們產品候選藥物的監管批准，並支付給我們取得或收購的產品候選藥物的授權人及其他第三方的潛在里程碑付款。本公司預期我們已核准藥物的產品銷售將持續每年增加；然而，由於來自Takeda及我們經銷商的大型定期訂單，我們的產品收入可能出現季度波動。此外，我們來自Takeda的產品收入是根據變動考量進行估計。若實際結果與我們的估計有所差異，我們將在這些差異被確認的期間進行調整。因此，我們的淨虧損可能在季度與年度之間出現顯著波動。

本公司預期將透過現有資本餘額、已核准藥物的收入，以及透過股票發行、債務融資或其他資金來源、合作、授權及其他類似安排來滿足未來的資金需求。然而，本公司可能無法在需要時以有利的條件或完全無法取得額外資金或進行這些其他安排。本公司若無法在需要時取得資金或進行這些其他安排，將對我們的財務狀況及我們追求業務計畫與策略的能力產生負面影響。若本公司無法在需要時取得額外資金，我們可能被迫延遲、限制、減少或終止一個或多個產品候選藥物的開發或未來商業化努力，或授予他人開發與行銷我們的產品候選藥物的權利，即使我們更傾向於自行開發與行銷這些產品候選藥物。
於2024年10月，本公司完成取得MRM-3379的授權。本公司在交易完成時支付一筆一次性不可退款的授權費750萬美元，並可能根據達成特定開發、監管及商業里程碑，支付最高達2億1,750萬美元的額外費用。

headings: 與本公司核准藥物商業化及產品候選藥物開發相關之風險
本公司業務之成功，在部分程度上取決於本公司能否以獲利方式行銷及銷售本公司核准之藥物。
若本公司無法取得及/或維持對本公司核准之藥物及任何未來產品候選藥物（若獲批准）足夠之給付及報銷，則本公司之商業成功可能受到嚴重阻礙。
本公司核准之藥物或任何一項產品候選藥物（若獲批准），可能無法在醫界（包括醫生、病人及其他相關人士）中獲得必要的市場接受度，以實現商業成功。
本公司可能面臨產品責任之風險，若有人對本公司提出索賠，且本公司針對該等索賠之保險覆蓋不足，則本公司可能需承擔重大賠償責任。
本公司業務在部分程度上取決於產品候選藥物之成功，而每項產品候選藥物在本公司可尋求監管機構批准及 potentially 開始商業銷售前，均需進行大量臨牀測試。
本公司已遭遇且可能持續遭遇在臨牀試驗中招募病患之延誤與困難，因此，本公司之臨牀發展活動可能延誤或受到其他不利影響。
本公司之臨牀試驗可能無法充分顯示產品候選藥物之安全性與有效性，這可能會導致監管機構批准及商業化之延誤或無法實現。
臨牀藥物開發涉及一個漫長且費用高昂的過程，結果具有不確定性，且較早期的研討會與試驗結果可能無法預測未來試驗的結果。
paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股股份涉及高度風險。您在決定是否購買、持有或出售本公司普通股股份前，應仔細考慮下列風險因素，以及本年度報告表10-K所載的其他資訊。上述任何風險事件的發生，可能會對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果及/或成長前景造成損害，或導致本公司實際結果與本年度報告表10-K中所作之預測性陳述，以及本公司未來可能作出的預測性陳述有重大差異。評估本公司業務時，應考慮所有所述風險因素。
本公司業務的成功，在部分程度上取決於本公司能否以獲利方式推廣已核准的藥物。本公司成功推廣已核准藥物，取決於多種因素，包括但不限於下列各項：
•本公司能否在美國、加拿大以及歐洲某些國家擴展並維持銷售團隊，並在這些地區及其他本公司產品可供使用的地區擴大分銷能力；
•本公司已核准藥物獲得足夠賠償及商業上可行的銷售價格；
•醫師、保險機構及患者是否接受本公司已核准藥物的效益、安全性與有效性，包括相對於其他替代性及競爭性治療方案；
•本公司已核准藥物持續具有可接受的安全性表現；
